rationale: Codebase-pin lens on 482bcd2f. Everything I ran is green and everything I spot-checked is honestly pinned: all 21 fixture-leg test functions pass (28s, real git, FILES ref backend, no mocks on the mechanism under test); the five assigned spot-reads (viii-a, ix, xii, xiv, xx) assert their NAMED scenarios with strong, specific checks (viii-a: marker==tip==C at stage=materialization, refusal names the interval-edit path, recovery line present, no rollback, worktree and edit content survive on disk, zero CompleteBead calls before the S-exit refusal; ix: same arc from the D marker; xii: marker published + tip NOT advanced + marker^==preTip, resume finishes the advance; xiv: rival CREATE-CAS wins, real publish refuses, rival OID survives unchanged; xx: no-marker route, tip pinned unchanged, exactly 2 CompleteBead calls). The ratchet extensions are honest registrations, not gate-weakening: guard/lint/executor/gitutil/validate all pass (count-exact ratchets), and I verified the argv-table claims against internal/gitutil/materialize.go line by line — RejectOptionLike gates are present exactly where the six new entries claim (ChangedFilesTree base/treeOID, MaterializeStageCommit tree/parent, UpdateRefCAS ref/newSHA/old, AdvanceBranchExpectedOld branch), ResetIndexOnlyMixed is all-literal, ClearMaterializationMarker's upstream-RevParseRef note is accurate, and the render-allowlist edit actually TIGHTENS a count (5 to 4) with an explanation. The ~10 adapted tests are sound retargets: c2/c3 now let the real AdvanceBranchExpectedOld ref move land, assert the tip genuinely advanced with the content present, then converge on re-invocation via the marker (crash-resume still pinned end to end; c5 unchanged in spirit); TestRun_DocSyncRefusesBeforeAnyMaterialization inverts the old gates-after-commit pin into zero-MaterializeStageCommit/zero-advance-before-refusal, which is the reorder's exact contract. The MockExecutor ChangedFilesTree-to-ChangedFiles fallback does not mask coverage: it only preserves pre-existing decision-logic tests, while the tree-leg MECHANICS are pinned by real-git legs — leg (i) would fail outright if the gate silently reverted to the committed-range diff (an untracked file is invisible to it), and leg (iii) pins the artifact-exclusion tree shape. ADR-0041 amendment tests 11/11 including OldGatesAfterCommitClaimGone. Why REQUEST_CHANGES despite all that: the single most security-relevant NEW behavior — the write-ahead resume skipping the panel gate entirely (complete.go step 2.25, guarded by resumeStage=="") — has no positive test anywhere. Every resume leg (viii-a, ix, xii, xiii, xv-xix) runs panel-less, and leg (xi) pins only the foreign-tip NEGATIVE. A regression that re-runs the panel gate on resume (deadlocking every kill-resume behind a stale-SHA refusal, breaking the protocol's own convergence promise) or one that widens the bypass would pass this entire matrix unchanged. For the bead whose falsifiability surface IS the leg matrix, that is a real ratchet hole with a ~20-line fix using in-file infrastructure.
concrete_changes_required: Add a fixture leg (leg-xi positive counterpart) pinning the panel+marker resume interplay: register a panel with ReviewedHeadSHA = the pre-run tip A (exactly as TestBead6Leg_xi does), kill after the first AdvanceBranchExpectedOld (marker==tip==C), then re-run WITHOUT any foreign commit and assert convergence (BeadClosed, ancestor-in-spec, marker cleared) — proving the write-ahead resume does NOT trip the stale-SHA gate even though tip != ReviewedHeadSHA, and pairing the existing foreign negative with the positive that makes the discriminator's bypass falsifiable.

findings.title: No positive test for the panel-gate bypass on write-ahead resume
findings.detail: complete.go step 2.25 skips the AUTHORITATIVE panel gate entirely when resumeStage != "" (the marker's existence proves a prior pass; write-ahead ordering makes that sound — marker publication happens strictly after the gate in runMaterialization). But no test in the package registers a panel AND resumes via the marker: legs viii-a/ix/xii/xiii/xv-xix are panel-less, leg xi covers only the foreign-commit stale-SHA negative, and c5's panel run resumes via merged-unclosed reconcile, not the discriminator. The bypass — the exact #186 cannot-launder boundary this bead exists to draw — is pinned only by a comment. See concrete_changes_required.

findings.title: internal/panel/gate.go:295 still describes the deleted CommitAll auto-commit mechanism
findings.detail: The panel dirty-tree guard's user-facing refusal reads "`mindspec complete` would auto-commit them past review (CommitAll); commit and re-panel, or revert". Post-reorder, complete never auto-commits via CommitAll — it snapshots and gates prospectively, then materializes via commit-tree. The refusal BEHAVIOR remains correct (uncommitted dirt would still be materialized into content the panel never reviewed), but in a state-honesty spec a guard message naming a mechanism this very bead deletes is doc-skew. internal/panel is outside the bead's touched-file set, so fixing here or filing a follow-up bead are both acceptable — but it must be one of the two.

findings.title: Leg-file inventory names a test function that does not exist
findings.detail: The inventory comment lists TestBead6Leg_viii_b_ResumeAfterClearingDirtConverges as a standalone test, but the viii-b convergence scenario is folded into TestBead6Leg_viii_a_ResumeKillBeforeReset_IntervalEditRefuses (its final section). The coverage is real; the inventory misleads a reader auditing name-to-leg completeness — the exact audit this file invites.

findings.title: Panel-conduct observation: stray probe file transiently in the shared bead worktree
findings.detail: During my run an UNTRACKED internal/complete/r4_flagship_probe_test.go (mtime after the artifact commit; not in 482bcd2f) sat in the shared bead worktree and made the package's -short suite FAIL (its own expectation of a doc-sync refusal hit the panel dirty-tree guard first — incidentally the trigger that surfaced the stale gate.go:295 message above). It was removed before I finished; final git status is clean and the tracked suite is green (the lone failure was that stray file). For the tally's conduct ledger, not a code finding.

deviations.A: Acceptable as landed, with a real disclosed cost: the operator's --commit-msg text now exists NOWHERE durable (pre-bead-6 it was the CommitAll subject; TestRun_AutoCommitMaterializesViaSnapshot correspondingly no longer asserts message text). The seam freeze at the prompt's literal 4-arg list explains the shape honestly. Recommend a follow-up (not this bead): carry the operator text in the M-stage commit BODY via a widened seam or second trailer, restoring the audit trail without touching the subject convention.
deviations.B: The coupling is sound GIVEN C, and I verified the load-bearing premise in code: the pre-S classification (runMaterialization's preUserDirt refusal) runs before the S snapshot, so the no-exclusion re-snapshot can only legitimately capture artifact refresh. Caveat I defer to R3/R6 per lens assignment: 'safe by construction' is really 'safe modulo a mutation landing in the pre-S-check-to-snapshot window' — and the post-hoc sExitContract cannot catch a swept-in edit (the worktree then matches D and reads clean). The defensive re-check is honest belt-and-suspenders for NEW dirt only, exactly as its own comment states.
deviations.C: From the pin lens: genuinely enforced, not just claimed. Legs viii-a and ix assert the invariant's every observable — refusal names the interval-edit path, content preserved byte-exact on disk, no rollback (tip pinned unchanged), no worktree removal, zero merge attempts before the refusal, then convergence after clearing. The plan's invariant (interval edits preserved-or-refused, never silently committed) is upheld at the moved (pre-S) primary enforcement point, and the ADR §3(i) staged-boundary classification tests pass (11/11 amendment pins, including the red-if-old-sentence-present pin).

Bead worktree left byte-identical (git status clean); scratch cleaned.
